subject: art-design
source_note: Structure follows the IB Diploma Visual Arts guide: theoretical, art-making and curatorial practices, assessed through the comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition. Component names are guide-accurate; connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (the IB does not publish these).

connections.why: Understanding context deepens the analysis of artworks
Analysis skills are applied directly in the comparative study
The comparative study examines the cultural context of works
Art-making approaches guide choices of media and technique
The journal records the experimentation behind artworks
Exploring media builds the skills used to make work
Developed skills enable refinement of artworks
The journal supplies evidence for the process portfolio
Experimentation is what the process portfolio documents
Refined artworks become the body of work exhibited
Selecting and organising work is the core of the exhibition
The exhibition must communicate intentions to viewers
Acknowledging influences links own work to other artists
Visual literacy underpins the analysis of artworks
Understanding the artist's role shapes how work is presented
